newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes seen mixed, ANS deal likely.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes seen mixed, ANS deal likely.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices were mixed in quiet Friday trade, with a consensus forming among traders that Alaska North Slope (ANS) sold late last week at $1.45 under February WTI, players said.
Arco was rumored to have sold the ANS cargo late last week, but the seller declined comment and a likely buyer -- Shell -- maintained its policy of not speaking to the press.
BP America, a key producer, was asking for $1.25 below March NYMEX, with bidders were as wide as $1.50 a barrel under.
With the diff for Alaska North Slope (ANS) tighter, outright prices rose eight cents, despite a flat prices for WTI.
The postings market for Line 63 crude was flat, after a deal got done at $1.00 over Buena Vista earlier this week.
No deals were reported for Line 63 on a fixed basis, but one trader claimed the discount stood about $2.20 to $2.30 below WTI.
Meanwhile, the market for California heavy crudes was talked lower than early week levels, with players hearing trades at 25 to 50 cents below postings.
Postings, the pricel index for California grades, fell Friday amid perceptions of ample supply .
Wilmington was heard done as high as 95 cents over postings earlier this week, a sharp increase over recent range of 40 to cents over postings.
Traders cited falling production at the Long Beach-area oil field.
